patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a persistent top utility/header area separated from the main article content; the desktop sketch especially has a distinct top bar with a search field and links that reads like a fixed utility bar.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Top navigation/search region should remain available while scrolling, likely pinned to the top across the long article page.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show scrolling states, so fixed vs static header is inferred from the persistent utility-bar treatment rather than directly depicted.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: A prominent rectangular input appears at the top of both mobile and desktop sketches, visually separated as a search/control field in the header area.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Search field should accept text and trigger a search action on submit; may also support focus styling and keyboard submission. If implemented like a sitewide search, it may optionally expose suggestions or route to results.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not indicate whether results are live/autocomplete or only submitted on Enter/button.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The top search field is an input-based form control intended for submission, implying at least basic handling of empty input, invalid states, or submit behavior.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: At minimum, validate/search-submit state for the header input and provide feedback if submission is empty or malformed, depending on implementation requirements.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit error states are drawn, so full validation messaging may be minimal.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a relatively low-JS article/detail page rather than a highly interactive application. The main interactive requirement across both viewports is the prominent header search form, with likely submit handling and basic validation/focus behavior. The desktop sketch more strongly suggests a persistent utility/header bar, while the mobile sketch remains mostly linear content with no explicit hamburger, tabs, accordion, modal, or load-more cues. Most of the page appears to be static reading content with a hero image and footer.
